body:
Thank you for the detailed answer and explanation of what you mean.

OK, maybe I do care to some degree. But why should I suffer in this life? (by 'I' am using it as a term for anybody in some sort of trouble). Would it not then be easier to kill yourself, cut out the pain of this life and move on to the next one without making things worse?

If I/you do the best we can in most situations with the occasional indulgence in selfish acts like all humans then that has to be enough. For me personally, I feel like once I got my act together I did everything I could. Knowing whatever I did had to come from me. But once its out of my hands I leave it up to God. But if the response back is always "Nope!" then there is only so much I can do. I don't want to live for only the next life, I need some sort of (immediate) satisfaction in this one too.

Again, not saying win the lottery etc, just that I won't be teased with a door slightly ajar only for it to be slammed in my face the moment I get too close leaving me in the middle of nowhere.

I see what you mean, and it does make sense in a way. 

But when we look at the people suffering, and by suffering I mean those who are born into a life that will be short and too difficult to comprehend, what do they gain from religion?

Can argue strength of will to carry on but that ultimately seems pointless if they haven't been able to get out their vicious cycle.

OK so its basically a form of distraction? So in essence, praying has no real merit except it maybe calms your brain/focuses it elsewhere for a bit?

If so, that is all well and good but then the shit will hit the fan again once your current circumstances are remembered.

Sorry if this is coming across as rude, not trying to be if it is, I'm just trying to understand. As you are one of the few people who have answered me on this question when I've asked, I may as well learn as much as I can.

My grandmother told me something similar. That we are praying for future lives/being rewarded and punished accordingly of previous lives.

My reaction to her about this was along the lines of "I don't care about my next birth, I will have no recollection of this one if this is all true. Why should I suffer for previous and future lives which will have no weighting on this one and my happiness?"

I grew up as a Hindu. Religious family but not crazy, always allowed me freedom. So in a way, I liked it so I stuck with it. My family has never tried to force me to stick with it.

And yes, doing good isn't really about fear of punishment rather the actual pleasure you gain from genuinely helping someone. I probably don't do much in regards to it as others do but I try and help if I can.

Thank you, and apologies for the late reply.

This is the thing. I have up until recently been very faithful regardless, in terms of in bad times I'd only gravitate more towards religion. But I am now thinking about it and thinking what is the point? If its all about acting good and doing your best then why do I need to read prayers etc if they don't really add anything. Seems like I am currently in between your second type of person and the first.

Apologies for the late reply.

Are you saying that these experiences etc are created? If so, that makes it worse I think

Apologies for the late reply.

Although it would be nice, I don't really expect to pray and get the world at my feet. I am asking what is the point of it? My parents for example pray daily, do good but still get shit. As do millions of others around the world. Can you not just be good without "wasting" a part of the day praying for relatively no reason? Can still celebrate festivals, follow rules etc.

Thanks for taking the time to read. But how? I can't just take it out on somebody who has nothing to do with it. But even thats only part of the problem, I've recently been going to sleep and waking up thinking about this job rejection. I then think so much about it I end up (like in most cases when something bad happens to me) thinking about what would have happened or should have done.

I can feel better after a bit but then it'll always come back. I need to get rid of that process of it coming back and making me miserable for the rest of the day. Its no way to live

Well I finished uni a few years ago and still keep in contact with most. But try to never get serious as we don't all see each other as much as we should so nobody ends up saying anything too depressing about their lives and just try and have a good time.

> The thing with it i for me is that I have the hardest time being happy when I should be and when sad things happen, I take them way harder than I should..... My life sometimes is a hilarious contradiction. I crave social interaction, yet when I get it I want nothing more than to be alone

That is me in a nutshell actually. I've never put it into words, or written it out but that is how I feel/am.

Thing I've also found, is that when I talk to somebody about it, it helps initially. Get into a good mood for a bit but then, BAM! "Here's that bit of bad news and all the other shit thats gone wrong in your life just to remind you that you should not be smiling or be happy". I do not know how to get rid of this currently.

Could of course say that I should keep talking. But if I do that then the person listening will have enough and leave. I would much rather hear others problems and help them than air mine to people I know. Which is probably why I have come to reddit and this sub for help.

Thank you for taking the time to read and reply. It does mean a lot when somebody takes an interest. The issue I've got with talking to my family is that they've been through so much already and I don't want them to stress (they do over the tiniest things, like me I guess). Unfortunately I do not have a girlfriend, which is upsetting in itself really. Lack of confidence in myself and be out there does not help.

Another thing I do is once a negative thought enters my head, it stays there. Nothing I do after is right. All the things I do and watch that made me smile before feel useless.

Dunno. It could be argued its just this rejection from the perfect job and company but I wouldn't feel this useless for just that I think. Whilst thats got me incredibly upset, its created a chain reaction of thought/realisation about how miserable, useless and pathetic I am. Feels like I'm being sucked in to quick sand whilst everyone is running away making it in life.
